Estimating tokens without a tokenizer is a trade-off. A real byte-pair encoder is accurate but heavy: it ships a large vocabulary file and costs real time on every call. A heuristic based on character counts is tiny and fast, but it drifts on unusual text such as long hexadecimal hashes, dense punctuation, or non-English scripts. For budgeting purposes we do not need exact counts. We need an estimate that is close enough on typical inputs and that errs slightly on the safe side, so that a message measured at 140 tokens really does fit under a cap of 150 when it reaches the model.
